chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Qutaybah al-Basri, from Abu Khalid al-Ajami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Five [qualities]: whoever does not have them, he does not have much that is beneficial/enjoyable: Religion, Intellect, Politeness/Etiquette, Freedom, and Good Character.

key_terms.الْحُرِّيَّةُ: Freedom (liberty from servitude or base desires)

ai.seo_question: What are the five essential qualities for a meaningful life according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to outline the five pillars of human perfection required for true benefit (*istimta'*). This enumeration bridges spiritual devotion (*al-din*) and rational capacity (*al-aql*) with social grace (*adab*), inner liberty (*al-hurriyyah*), and moral conduct (*husn al-khuluq*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of intellect and ethics. The absence of these traits renders one's existence devoid of substantial utility or pleasure.
